classification.recommended_terminology: finite-level dimension of the totient k-kernel
classification.terminology_boundary: The k-kernel and k-regularity are Allouche--Shallit terminology. Finite-level dimension and filtration-compatible basis are literal descriptions, not located named invariants.
nearest_prior_work: Martin (2006), Theorem 1, proves arbitrarily strong simultaneous orderings of Euler-totient values on pairwise nonproportional positive affine forms; the linear-independence step is a direct corollary.
Coons (2010), Theorem 3.2, proves that the Euler totient sequence is not k-regular for every k>=2, already implying that its full integer-valued k-kernel has infinite rational span.
Allouche and Shallit (1992) introduce the ring/module framework of k-regular sequences and the k-kernel viewpoint, but do not give this finite-level rank formula.
classification.attribution: Credit Martin for the decisive affine-totient domination mechanism, Allouche--Shallit for the framework, and Coons for prior nonregularity/infinite-rank knowledge. Attribute only the exact k^e+1 filtration law, the displayed bases, and the complete reductions to the local ordinary proof, with base 2 separately identified as Lean-checked.
classification.mathematical_interest: A clean quantitative refinement of nonregularity: the bounded-depth kernel span has maximal-looking linear growth in the number of level-e sections plus one persistent lower-level direction. The result is concise and reusable, but its independence argument is an application rather than a new analytic mechanism.
classification.reusable_scope: Kernel filtrations of arithmetic functions where same-level affine sections can be separated by a domination theorem and divisibility supplies exact cross-level reductions.
classification.why_it_matters: It replaces the coarse statement 'the kernel has infinite rank' by an exact dimension law and complete relation model, while preventing that refinement from being misreported as new nonregularity or as an irrationality result.

primary_sources.title: Simultaneous inequalities among values of the Euler phi-function
primary_sources.author: Greg Martin
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Theorem 1: for positive affine forms a_i n+b_i with nonzero pairwise cross-determinants and any C>0, prescribed simultaneous phi-ratio inequalities hold on a set of positive lower density.
primary_sources.supports: The domination argument that makes totient sequences on pairwise nonproportional affine forms rationally linearly independent.
primary_sources.does_not_support: k-kernel terminology, the rank k^e+1, either explicit basis, or the relation normal form.

primary_sources.title: (Non)Automaticity of number theoretic functions
primary_sources.author: Michael Coons
primary_sources.venue: Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 22 (2010), 339-352
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Theorem 3.2: the Euler totient function is not k-regular for any k>=2.
primary_sources.supports: Prior knowledge of non-k-regularity and hence, for this integer-valued kernel, failure of finite-dimensional rational kernel span.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Any finite-level dimension, explicit basis, or complete cross-level relation formula.

primary_sources.title: The ring of k-regular sequences
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The paper introduces k-regular sequences through finite generation of the module generated by the k-kernel and develops their ring structure.
primary_sources.supports: The canonical framework and terminology in which the totient sections and their spans live.

mechanism_comparison.known_global_fact: Coons already excludes finite generation of the full totient k-kernel module.
mechanism_comparison.load_bearing_input: Martin's arbitrary-factor simultaneous inequalities imply linear independence for totient values on pairwise nonproportional affine forms.
mechanism_comparison.elementary_reductions: Multiplicativity collapses sections whose residues share powers of k and reduces all bounded levels to a top-level family plus phi(n).
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: Combining the reductions with Martin's separation gives dimension k^e+1, two bases, and every rational relation among bounded-level sections.
mechanism_comparison.formal_boundary: Only k=2 has the stated Lean coverage; the all-k result remains an ordinary, unrefereed proof.
